transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-10 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Luca Morales (Redwood), Priya Singh (Asteria NetOps), Tom Reyes (Asteria SRE), Elena Park (Asteria Security), Marcus Liu (Asteria CTO)

Summary: mid-pilot sync to review results from last 72 hour bakeout and investigate intermittent wirepath hops causing p99 spikes.

[00:00] Maya: ok, hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll kick off, I see folks on the call. quick agenda — wirepath traces, kernel patch status, security Qs, next steps.
[00:22] Marcus: yep, thanks Maya. we had some user-facing tail latency at 3am UTC last night, so want to get to root cause.
[00:35] Priya: i pulled the traceroutes we ran, there are a couple of weird AS jumps between our vpc peering and Redwood's ingress in eu-west-1.
[00:50] Jordan: when you say AS jumps, do you mean a provider handoff, or a load-balancer redirect? sometimes the netpath looks like a cross-connect redirect, which explains a 200-300ms spike.
[01:10] Tom: looks like both, sometimes it's a handoff to a transit provider; other times it's a flapping path, which aligns with the p99 spikes we saw.
[01:30] Maya: ok, can you call out timestamps from your CSV? we have a shared sheet link in the deck — (link) https://redwood.shared/asteria-wirepath-bakeout — note: link is redacted in minutes but the file exists.
[01:50] Priya: yeah, row 234-256 show the worst cluster: 2027-11-09 02:14 to 02:27, p99 jumped to 1.6s. p50 was fine.
[02:10] Luca: that's useful; that pattern usually indicates queueing at an intermediate hop, not server-side compute. but we saw some server-side tail too when kv cache warmed up.
[02:30] Tom: kv cash? you mean KV cache?
[02:36] Luca: yes sorry, kv cache — the auto prefix caching. the warm-up behavior increased local compute for a short period last week.
[02:50] Elena: from a security perspective we flagged the mtls / PSK handshake behaviour during the flaps; logs show occasional re-key requests that correlate with the same window.
[03:10] Jordan: hmm rekeys could cause handshake renegotiation delays — are you using short-lived session keys?
[03:20] Elena: Asteria has a PSK rotation every 6 minutes on the prod egress appliance. maybe that's too short when combined with a path change.
[03:40] Maya: ok that's a good lead — Priya, can you capture the exact rekey windows and align them with the p99 spikes?
[03:50] Priya: yes i'll annotate the trace sheet.
[04:05] Marcus: also, the MTU mismatch theory — in one of the hops we saw a fragmentation flag. could an MTU config be causing retransmits?
[04:20] Jordan: absolutely, if there's an off-by-1 MTU you can see retransmits leading to tail latency. we recommend 1500 across the chain or jumbo agreed end-to-end; mismatched MTU between VPC peer and on-prem routers can be nasty.
[04:45] Tom: we have an MTU 9000 between some internal hosts but the cross-connect is 1500. we should standardize.
[05:00] Luca: for the pilot we can instrument a pathprobe with explicit pmtu discovery and packet captures. i'll add the runtime flag to log PMTU events.
[05:20] Maya: great. quick status on the kernel compat patch Jordan was testing?
[05:30] Jordan: yes, patch v0.9.2 applied to staging cluster last night. initial metrics look promising: p95 down 12%, p99 down about 8% — but we saw two exceptions tied to route flaps.
[05:50] Priya: can you share the exact patch and command? we want to replicate on our mirrored staging.
[06:00] Jordan: sure — patch is in the repo, link in the notes — i'll paste in chat after the call. it toggles a different I/O path for the kv cache and disables a noisy kernel prefetch.
[06:20] Tom: the kv cache toggles are interesting — do you have a recommended set of flags for low-latency workloads?
[06:30] Luca: for bursty workloads we recommend prefix_cache=on, kv_cache_eviction=LRU-aggressive, and continuous_batching=enabled with max_batch_size tuned to 16-32. but that trades off a little CPU.
[06:50] Marcus: that CPU tradeoff is fine if it keeps p99 predictable. cost is less critical than SLAs for us.
[07:05] Maya: noted. Elena, any blockers on the security questionnaire we sent?
[07:15] Elena: a couple items — KMS workflow (we asked about HSM-backed keys), audit log retention, and SSO mapping for RBAC. we need clear answers for compliance.
[07:33] Maya: we have a security pack at https://redwood.dev/security that covers SOC2, HSM/KMS patterns, and audit schemas. i'll attach it after. for HSM-backed keys, Redwood supports customer-managed KMS integrations and can do an HSM-backed signer via AWS CloudHSM or equivalent.
[07:55] Elena: ok we'll need to see the exact KMS call flow and who can access plaintext.
[08:05] Jordan: we can produce a flow diagram and an exported minimal trace that shows the KMS envelope flow without secrets.
[08:18] Priya: back to wirepath — we also instrumented TCP retransmit counts; there's a small bump in retransmits just before the p99 spike. likely a windowing or MTU issue.
[08:35] Tom: that aligns with the fragmentation flag we saw.
[08:45] Luca: to be thorough: we'll run a three-pronged approach this week — 1) kernel compatibility patch on test clusters, 2) PMTU probes + packet captures during a scheduled timeslot, 3) test rekey timing adjustments on Asteria's egress to see if 6min rotation is the culprit.
[09:05] Maya: agree. schedule wise, can we get patch + capture in the next 48 hours?
[09:12] Priya: yes, we'll allocate a maintenance window on 2027-11-12 02:00-03:00 UTC to run path probes.
[09:20] Jordan: i'll push the patch to the test cluster tonight and run a 24h soak. Luca will enable the pmtu logging flags.
[09:30] Marcus: perfect. what's the acceptance criteria for the smoke test?
[09:38] Maya: acceptance: p99 below 600ms baseline during the smoke window, no more than two isolated spikes above 1s, and no reconnects caused by KMS renegotiation.
[09:55] Elena: also: no audit log gaps and KMS calls searchable by request id.
[10:05] Tom: noted. what about fallback routing — if we detect a path with >1s latency for more than 30s, can Redwood auto-failover to the secondary region?
[10:20] Jordan: yes, we can configure smart routing to consider latency thresholds and route to a compatible model in a second region; tradeoff is cross-region egress cost and slightly higher cold-start for different cache state.
[10:40] Maya: that's an option but we'll try to fix the primary path first. Marcus: any concerns?
[10:48] Marcus: want to avoid cross-region lawyering and data residency surprises. Don't want EU traffic leaving region.
[11:00] Elena: yes, data residency will block cross-region fallback; prefer intra-region alternatives or in-region redundant paths.
[11:12] Jordan: understood — we can configure fallback to a regional sibling or warm standby in the same region.
[11:25] Priya: quick question — do you need any specific firewall ports opened for the pmtu probe or kernel debug logs?
[11:33] Luca: mainly TCP 443 egress to our collector, plus ephemeral ports for tracing. we'll put a minimal list in the notes.
[11:45] Tom: we'll need the ip ranges and short-lived certs for the smoke test.
[12:00] Maya: i'll provide ip ranges and an ephemeral cert generation script.
[12:10] Jordan:on the patch, early stage numbers: during a 6h run we saw average token latency unchanged but fewer 95/99 outliers; I can paste the graphs. heads-up: transcription of the graphs in the doc might get messy, but the raw CSV is in the shared drive.
[12:32] Priya: i noticed a curious artifact in one trace where hop 4 sometimes reports zero TTL decrement — could that be a router misreporting?
[12:44] Jordan: most likely, some middleboxes hide TTL changes; it's why we rely on combined tcpdump and pathtrace to get ground truth.
[12:57] Luca: regarding instrumentation, i'm going to enable full traces on a 1% sample for 48h to capture a richer set of anomalies. that will add some overhead but should be minimal.
[13:14] Marcus: that's fine. as long as it's sampled and not full traffic.
[13:22] Elena: security note: sampled pcaps should be scrubbed; don't include payloads or PII.
[13:32] Luca: agreed, we'll sanitize and only keep headers, retransmit counters, timings.
[13:40] Maya: great. next: KMS flow — Elena said you want a diagram?
[13:47] Jordan: yes, plus a short writeup that maps roles -> who can call decrypt and where plaintext exists in memory, retention windows.
[14:00] Elena: also, do you support HSM signing for keywrap operations?
[14:08] Maya: yes, we can integrate with customer-managed HSM via AWS CloudHSM or HashiCorp with an approved KMS provider; we'll show the TLS handshake flow and KMS envelope steps.
[14:22] Tom: timeline for that?
[14:27] Maya: we can sketch the flow now, and a full integration runbook will take ~2 weeks to validate end-to-end with your HSM vendor.
[14:37] Marcus: two weeks is fine if we can run interim smoke tests.
[14:45] Priya: agreeing — let's keep the smoke test focused on network and kernel patch first, then second week validate KMS/HSM integration.
[15:00] Jordan: for visibility, i'll add span IDs to the trace so we can correlate KMS calls and handshake times with p99 events.
[15:12] Priya: excellent.
[15:20] Maya: any concerns about cost or billing for the extra sampled traces?
[15:27] Marcus: keep it minimal; we don't need 100% sampling. 1% for 48 hours is fine. if costs balloon we'll revisit.
[15:38] Elena: quick compliance quirk — audit retention policy needs to be 7 years for one of our regs. do you support custom retention for export?
[15:48] Maya: yes we can export audit logs to your sink with configurable retention policies; retention in Redwood's console is configurable up to X years — i'll confirm the max retention and policy doc.
[16:05] Tom: coming back to fallback: if region fallback is disabled for residency, can you still do multi-path within region (e.g., AZ failover)?
[16:18] Jordan: yep, multi-AZ redundant routing is default. we can also pin to a particular AZ for performance tests, but autobalance helps.
[16:30] Priya: want to run a short experiment: route traffic through an alternate egress appliance to see if path improves. we can cut 30% of traffic for 20 minutes and measure.
[16:42] Luca: sounds good. risk low and informative.
[16:50] Marcus: let's confirm exact windows in the next 24h.
[16:58] Maya: action points recap: Jordan pushes kernel patch and shares commands; Luca enables pmtu and 1% full traces; Priya runs path probes and shares tcpdumps sanitized; Elena and Maya align on KMS diagram; schedule smoke test week of 11/22.
[17:20] Tom: can you also include a short runbook on rollback steps if patch causes regressions? we need a simple reroll command.
[17:30] Jordan: yes i will add a one-click rollback script and test it in staging.
[17:40] Priya: one more data point — our ops noticed a tiny bump in connection refused errors when your runtime did a cache compaction. could that cause brief reconnects?
[17:54] Luca: cache compaction triggers ephemeral backpressure on accept queues — we have mitigations but i'll tune thresholds to be less aggressive for your workload.
[18:08] Marcus: nice.
[18:12] Elena: last question, do you store any request payload logs by default?
[18:18] Maya: by default we store minimal request metadata; payload logging is opt-in and can be disabled. all logs are encrypted at rest.
[18:30] Marcus: okay that's acceptable.
[18:36] Maya: ok let's align on timeline: Jordan to share patch and csv by 11/11 EOD, Luca to enable pmtu and tracing by 11/12, Priya to run path probe 11/12 02:00-03:00 UTC and drop tcpdumps in shared sheet, Elena to send security questions responses by 11/16, and schedule the smoke test week of 11/22.
[19:05] Tom: i'll send calendar invites once Priya confirms the 02:00 window.
[19:13] Priya: confirmed.
[19:20] Maya: ok last thing — any blockers on our side to proceed?
[19:25] Marcus: none. we all good.
[19:30] Maya: great thanks everyone. i'll follow up with the links and the security pack.
[19:37] Jordan: i'll paste the patch link and the rollback script in the notes.
[19:42] Luca: i'll post instrumentation flags.
[19:45] Elena: we'll start the compliance review and get back with the KMS specifics.
[19:50] Maya: thanks all; meeting adjourned.

Post-meeting notes:
- shared artifacts: kernel patch repo link (private), pmtu probe script, sanitized tcpdump upload location.
- acceptance criteria and smoke test checklist saved to the pilot tracker (internal).
- next sync tentatively scheduled after smoke test for 2027-11-23.

End of transcript.
